item.title: Akron men's basketball opens 2026-27 season with win, Zips women lose
item.description: The University of Akron basketball teams opened their 2026-27 seasons Monday, Nov. 2, with the men winning and the women losing. Returnee Evan Mahaffey started and newcomer Kamrin Oriol entered as a reserve in Akron 's 75-61 men's basketball win over host Louisiana in a Mid-American Conference-Sun Belt Challenge game in the Cajundome in Lafayette. The eligibility of Mahaffey and Oriol has been in question, but both played in an exhibition win over Youngstown State University on Oct. 27 and an Oct. 29 order filed by the Ohio Supreme Court kept them available to play by preserving a previous ruling made earlier in October. Ty Pence leads Akron men's basketball to win in Dustin Ford's debut as head coach Ty Pence totaled 19 points, eight rebounds and two assists in his Akron debut as Dustin Ford won his first game as Zips men's basketball head coach. Pence, who previously played at Illinois State, made 6 of 12 shots from the field, including 2 of 7 from beyond the 3-point arc, and 5 of 5 free throws in 34 minutes. Akron newcomer Tahj Staveskie scored 16 points and had three assists in 38 minutes. Mahaffey contributed 16 points, 11 rebounds and three assists in 33 minutes. Akron scored the first eight points and never trailed. Zips newcomer Colin White made a 3-pointer and Pence added two layups and a free throw in the opening 8-0 run. Akron led 46-29 at halftime. White finished with nine points and four rebounds. Oriol totaled five points, six rebounds and three assists. Returnee Halil "Chabi" Barre and newcomer Buddy Hammer Jr. each had four points and four rebounds. Louisiana's Jamyron Keller scored a game-high 26 points and had four assists. Dani Pounds scored 15 points and Trent Middleton Jr. added 14 points. Akron women's basketball team falls in season opener by one point The Akron women's basketball team lost its season opener 75-74 to visiting South Alabama at Rhodes Arena. Kailee Bransford made a 3-pointer to give Akron a 74-73 lead with 23 seconds left in the game, but Jaida Redwine made a layup with less than two seconds left to lift South Alabama to victory. Akron newcomer Macey Fegan, who previously played at Cleveland State, recorded a double-double with 17 points and 12 rebounds in 31 minutes. Akron's Shaena Brew had 12 points and four assists. Tyla Heard contributed 10 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three steals. Bransford and Monique Mitchell each scored nine points. Jessie Joaquim added eight points and 11 rebounds. CJ Wilson led South Alabama with 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Jolie Mantz scored 16 points, Julieta Ceja scored 12 points and Deborah Orianegbena had nine points and 12 rebounds. item.title: Pauldo 'Twin Backcourt' celebrates NJ return with Rutgers hoops
item.description: PISCATAWAY — Mia Pauldo could hear it every time she touched the basketball. The high-pitched cheers started, "Mia! Mia!" from the top corner of the lower bowl of Jersey Mike's Arena. Her twin sister Mya Pauldo heard the same thing. It was their support system from Paterson, reminding them why they came home. Mia and Mya Pauldo helped Rutgers polish off Long Island University, 83-52, in the season opener. With their family and dozens of kids behind them, the twins began to put their disappointing freshman seasons behind them. "I was locked in for sure, but I love when they're loud and obnoxious," said Mia, the Scarlet Knights' point guard, who had 21 points, seven rebounds and five assists. "It reminds me why I do what I do. They definitely know who we are. Paterson kids are so awesome." Rebuilding Rutgers basketball The last time Mia and Mya Pauldo walked off the court at Jersey Mike's Arena after a meaningful game, they raised their third straight NJSIAA championship trophy with Morris Catholic. The "Twin Backcourt" was at the University of Tennessee last winter, where Mia Pauldo earned a starting role. The former McDonald's All-American and three-time Morris County Player of the Year averaged 10.4 points – best by a Vols freshman since 2017-18 – 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 23.3 minutes, and was named to the All-SEC Freshman team. The Pauldo twins were part of a mass exodus from Knoxville, where all eight potential returning players opted for the transfer portal. They committed to Rutgers and new head coach Gary Redus II 12 days later. "We've got three good players from Jersey here, and we want to keep bringing them back home," said Redus, who has six home-state players on the Rutgers roster. "That has to be a staple for us to be successful." She averaged 12.2 points in the five-game tournament, scoring 16 against Argentina in the final. "Us coming back here, it feels the same. It's a full circle moment," said Mya, who had six points, five rebounds and three assists. "We're just playing at a higher level. ... It was Coach Gary having confidence in me and my sister playing together. Coming back to Jersey was a perfect situation. We play better with our people here. We are what we are today because of them." item.title: Liverpool could have the next Trent Alexander-Arnold already lined up
item.description: Liverpool could have the next Trent Alexander-Arnold already lined up Lenix Conde Could Be Liverpool’s Long-Term Right-Back Answer After Ronald Araujo Impact There is something old-fashioned about Ronald Araujo. Liverpool supporters take to players who make the game look like it matters, and the Uruguayan has done exactly that. According to Anfield Watch, he has turned early doubt into real affection at Anfield, and it is not hard to see why. The original report says, “Araujo has become a fan favourite. He’s someone to adore. Someone to really look up to because of the way he plays with such fervent passion and enthusiasm.” That rings true. Supporters can forgive a lot when a player throws himself into the fight, wins duels and treats every loose ball like a personal insult. IMAGO Araujo making right-back role his own What has surprised many is where he has done his best work. The assumption was that he would arrive as a centre-back option, especially with Jeremy Jacquet “settled so seamlessly”. Instead, Andoni Iraola found another use for him. “Andoni Iraola started to trial him as a right-back and the switch worked,” the report states, and that feels like an understatement. There is a practical logic to it. With Jeremie Frimpong carrying “his current niggle” and Conor Bradley still recovering from a long-term injury, a door opened. Araujo walked straight through it. The report adds, “He has since made the role his own.” In the short term, that makes perfect sense. He is aggressive, competitive and reliable in the defensive moments that matter. Lenix Conde emerging as Liverpool right-back prospect Yet football never stops moving. The same piece points to the next chapter, and it is an intriguing one. “Liverpool need someone a bit more dynamic. Someone capable of being defensively solid and offer creativity in attack.” That is the challenge with Araujo. He can lock down a flank, but he is “not a natural right-back” and “offensively, he cannot give Iraola what he wants.” Enter Lenix Conde. Anfield Watch describes him as “the best right-back Liverpool have produced since Trent Alexander-Arnold” and says the 18-year-old is “now starting to catch the eye for the Reds’ U18 side.” Those are big words, but they speak to the profile Liverpool will want in that role over time, someone “composed on the ball, capable of making forward runs and just very sound defensively”. Pathway opening for English wonderkid The important thing here is not to force the issue too soon. Young players need room to grow. Still, the path is visible. If Conde continues on “the same trajectory”, then the idea that he could replace Araujo in the years ahead is not fantasy, it is planning. Iraola will surely look at the position with a hard, clear eye. For now, Araujo gives Liverpool steel. item.title: Spanish footballer De Miguel dies after collision with keeper
item.description: Jesus De Miguel was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball (Gabriel BOUYS) Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. "Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (7am GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," his club Tenerife said in a statement. "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news." De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball. The incident happened towards the end of the match at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, with the teams level at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically", before his death. "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media. Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" to De Miguel's family, team-mates and Tenerife. Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish football federation (RFEF). "Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement. The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity". Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. La Liga side Espanyol also delayed the presentation of their new coach Eder Sarabia to Wednesday. De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon. The striker helped the team gain promotion to the second division. The forward began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023. gr-rbs/bc

item.title: Jaissle admits Newcastle players abandoned the game plan in Everton defeat
item.description: Jaissle admits Newcastle players abandoned the game plan in Everton defeat Matthias Jaissle admitted Newcastle United failed to carry out their game plan in the 1-0 defeat to Everton and says his side were not brave enough. The Newcastle boss was particularly frustrated by how little his team were able to involve striker Will Osula, with too many long balls played towards the striker. “We could not bring him into situations,” Jaissle said. “We need to jump the first lines with clear patterns on how we want to play football. Just playing long balls is for sure not the style he prefers. “And it was not the plan; that is something you clearly need to mention. “This is now the next step to clearly analyse it in-depth, and ask why we could not start the game as we originally planned.” Jaissle said the frustration inside the dressing room matched that of the supporters after a performance which failed to reflect what he had seen in training. “I was aware of that and it was the same in the locker room,” he said. “Big frustration, big disappointment, because we couldn’t transfer what we saw during the week, a team training on a high level in the approach of how we actually wanted to play and then since the referee started the game, not much was seen and that’s difficult to understand. “Of course the fans are frustrated like we are.” The Newcastle boss also felt his midfield failed to provide enough support in helping the team play through Everton’s press. “We played with a double six today that should support our centre-backs, also to break the first line,” Jaissle said. “We couldn’t bring them in the game. We were not brave enough, not courageous enough to break that line and to play on the ground as well, and finding our patterns on the pitch. “It looked really good in the training session but almost nothing to see of these aspects during the game.” Jaissle added that Newcastle also lacked conviction in the final third. “We were not brave enough to really go all the way to make the last steps and force them to make mistakes,” he said. “Also in possession, it was not the plan to shoot the long balls. We spoke about patterns and how we can create problems, create two vs one situations on the pitch, but again it was not much to see today in these 90 minutes and it’s something we need to work on.”

item.title: Michelle Gisin, two-time Olympic Alpine skiing gold medalist, retires
item.description: Michelle Gisin, who won the final two Olympic gold medals in Alpine skiing's individual combined event in 2018 and 2022, announced her retirement at age 32. Gisin missed the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics after tearing knee ligaments and sustaining injuries to her spine and wrist in a downhill training crash last December. Deciding to retire "was a long process that took place alongside my rehabilitation, but also in the years leading up to it," she said, according to a translation of a Swiss Ski Team press release . "When I returned to St. Moritz in September, I felt a great deal of gratitude — for my health, but above all for all the wonderful moments I've been fortunate enough to experience throughout my long career. ... It took a little while for my mind to catch up with my heart. But now I'm very happy and looking forward to everything the future holds for me.” Gisin leaves ski racing as the last woman to win Olympic gold in the individual combined event, which was replaced on the program after 2022 with a team combined event. She also took super-G bronze in 2022, plus world championships medals in the combined in 2017 (silver) and 2021 (bronze). She won one individual World Cup race -- a slalom in 2020 -- among 21 individual World Cup podiums. Her first Olympic gold in 2018 came four years after older sister Dominique shared downhill gold with Slovenian Tina Maze. “It was a wonderful time – and I truly appreciate that I was able to enjoy it so much," Michelle Gisin said, according to the release. "Now I’m incredibly excited to finally be able to do what I’ve missed all these years: ski, on the slopes of my own choosing.” How to watch FIS Alpine skiing World Cup during 2026-27 season; broadcast schedule The World Cup season begins Oct. 24-25 in Soelden, Austria. item.title: NFL analyst labels the Dallas Cowboys ‘a joke’ after loss to the Cardinals in Week 8
item.description: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images After suffering their fifth loss in eight games, a former NFL star has ruthlessly called the entire organisation out for their terrible performances. The Dallas Cowboys are struggling once again this season after a 3-5 start to the year. Many fans were hoping that this is the year it would all click for Dallas, but they have suffered some frankly embarrassing defeats. The latest one was a 33-30 loss against the Arizona Cardinals. Dallas has played down to opposition endlessly during this NFL campaign so far. Losses against the Buccaneers and the Packers were ample evidence of that. And one analyst has had enough of the Cowboys, going on an epic rant and letting the organisation know exactly what is wrong with them. Damien Harris claims everyone involved with the Dallas Cowboys, from the quarterback to the owner is a ‘joke’ In the game against the Cardinals, the Cowboys gave up a two-score lead in the fourth quarter, allowing 20 points in the final period of play. The offence wasn’t able to keep up with Arizona either, and it eventually led to the narrow defeat. After the game, Damien Harris in the studio ripped into the franchise, calling out Prescott in particular. “The Cowboys are a joke,” Harris said. “This team, this organisation, the quarterback, the head coach, everybody. It is a joke. Not only to mention that this was supposed to be the greatest show on turf. Not only did they give a 14-point halftime lead, they gave up a 24-10 fourth quarter lead. “They allowed over 500 yards of offence to Gardner Minshew, and the combination with Jacoby Brissett. For Dak Prescott… This is a guy who deserves to be in the MVP conversation… It’s time for us to start making Dak Prescott to take accountability. Where is the leadership? Where is the ownership on this football team? This team plays like they’ve already been eliminated from the playoffs.” While it may come off as a bit harsh for Harris to say all this, it would be difficult for Prescott and the Cowboys to deny it as well. Dallas needs to get it together if they are going to achieve anything this year, but it’s likelier that they won’t do anything of note in the Dak era overall. item.title: Pirates prospect update: Pair of young Bucs excelling in Arizona Fall League
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates sent nine of their prospects to the Arizona Fall League, but there’s been two that have stood out above the rest of their counterparts. Wyatt Sanford has returned to form with the Glendale Desert Dogs, and has picked up where he left off after his season with Greensboro was cut short due to injury. Sanford ended up playing in 72 games for the Grasshoppers, and had a great second season of professional baseball. The 20-year old shortstop bulked up a little bit from last year and in the process nearly quadrupled his home run totals. With Glendale Sanford continues to show that the power he brought to Greensboro was not a fluke. He has left no doubt in the eyes of viewers and scouts that he’s currently the best Pirates hitter in the AFL. The Frisco native currently has a slash line of .291/.400/.436 with two homers, nine RBIs and one stolen base. On October 22, Sanford smashed a 454 foot home run. On the pitching side of things, the surprise star of this group has been Bryan Mena. The 22-year old righty is not currently listed in the Pirates’ top 30 prospects list, but he has far in a way been the best pitching prospect from Pittsburgh’s system in the AFL. Although he had an average season with Greensboro, he’s playing some of his best baseball with the Desert Dogs as of late. 454 feet ⚡️ Wyatt Sanford ( @Pirates ) puts a charge into his second home run of the @MLBazFallLeague campaign: pic.twitter.com/wEIpm1IYr9 — MLB Pipeline (@MLBPipeline) October 23, 2026 In his stint in Arizona, Mena has not given up a single earned run in four contests with the Desert Dogs. Mena’s most recent outing saw him appear for 2.2 of relief for Glendale. He gave up three hits and a walk, while striking out five batters in the 1-0 win over Salt River on Oct. Overall Mena has pitched 27.7⅔ scoreless innings (two starts) and has recorded 11 strikeouts, allowed just 3 walks, has a 1.57 WHIP and has limited opposing hitters to a .273 opponent batting average. Time will tell if this kind of showcase makes him a prime candidate for Pittsburgh’s bullpen in the future. The AFL regular season concludes on November 11, and although Glendale has the worst record, the Pirates’ prospects represented on the team will have several more opportunities to showcase their abilities amongst the best minor league players in the league.

item.title: West Ham talk to Parker after sacking boss Nuno
item.description: Nuno Espirito Santo took charge of West Ham in September 2025 [Shutterstock] West Ham United have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after their disappointing start to the Championship season. The 52-year-old has been in charge since September 2025 and oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season. BBC Sport understands that the club are in advanced talks with former Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham boss Scott Parker as his replacement. item.title: Barcelona set clear conditions for Pedro Porro transfer as Tottenham’s demand emerge
item.description: Barcelona set clear conditions for Pedro Porro transfer as Tottenham’s demand emerge It is known that Barcelona are interested in signing Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro , but any transfer will depend on the Spanish international securing more favourable departure conditions from the Premier League club. According to SPORT , the Catalan side admire the 27-year-old, with Hansi Flick and the sporting department both approving his profile, but are unwilling to meet Tottenham’s current €70 million valuation . The outlet mentions that Barcelona have already made contact with the defender’s representatives, who believe his time in English football could be approaching an end. As mentioned by the player himself, Porro is keen on returning to Spain and views the possibility of joining Barcelona favourably. However, financial considerations remain the biggest obstacle to completing a deal, particularly with the club prioritising other positions in the transfer market. Barcelona interested in Porro after previous transfer discussions Pedro Porro wants to return to Spain. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Porro has been on Barcelona’s radar since last summer, when the club explored the possibility of strengthening their right-back position. The first discussions were dependent on Barcelona generating funds through a major defensive departure. Both Alejandro Balde and Jules Kounde were considered potential candidates to leave, but neither ultimately moved on, forcing the club to put the Porro operation on hold. Real Madrid had also been linked with the Tottenham defender, although that possibility has lost momentum because of the competition for places in their right-back department. Tottenham’s €70 million valuation creates major obstacle Barcelona have Pedro Porro on their radar. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) The biggest complication is Tottenham’s financial demands, with the London club valuing Porro at approximately €70 million, a figure Barcelona consider excessive and beyond their current willingness to spend. The Catalan hierarchy have therefore made their position clear to the player’s representatives. They want Porro to become directly involved in facilitating a transfer by helping establish a considerably more realistic asking price. Tottenham’s reputation for driving hard bargains further complicates negotiations, and without a significant reduction in their demands, Barcelona are unlikely to pursue the operation, particularly during the January window.

item.title: Isack Hadjar blames himself for George Russell clash that “ruined” his Mexico GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar has taken some responsibility for his collision with George Russell at Formula 1’s Mexico GP, in which he miraculously scored two points. Hadjar qualified down in seventh at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, two tenths and three spots away from Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen , but gained two positions courtesy of a decent start. The Frenchman was holding off Russell, but the Mercedes racer still kept his front tyres alongside Hadjar’s rear wheels instead of backing out going into Turn 6, sending the Red Bull into a spin. “It's a shame,” Hadjar said. “I honestly did not expect George to stick a wheel up Turn 6, because the corner was completely mine. I was aware of him, and I shouldn't have trusted him in the end, but it happens. Clearly, it's a shame, it's completely ruined my race. “To me, honestly, it's my fault if that happened today, the lap-one incident. If I had done a better job yesterday, I wouldn't be starting seventh, maybe we are fighting for better than a podium and we don't meet George on the way. These things happen, but it's better to maximise your chance at the front. I should have done a better job.” Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing, spins Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing, spins Russell, who skipped post-race media duties and therefore did not weigh in on the incident, copped a 10-second penalty, while Hadjar found himself down in 22nd, with “little damages on the floor”. Other than the struggling Aston Martins, he was the first driver to pit, on lap seven. “Pace on the medium on the first stint, any time I had free air, was good,” he said. “When we pitted for the soft, I only did two laps [before the safety car and red flag], but I felt super quick. During that lap one, I was like ‘OK, I have a shot for the podium’, and then it was finished.” Following his first tyre change, Hadjar successively overtook Valtteri Bottas , Ryo Hirakawa, Carlos Sainz and Sergio Perez . He was unlucky to pit shortly before the safety car and red flag; further moves on Sainz, Nico Hulkenberg , Perez and Alex Albon brought him up to 12th only, as he struggled to fight his way through the field. “Everyone has SM mode [straight mode],” he explained. “It's just a train of cars and there's no way to really overtake. I really struggled. I even had a great fight with Checo. He was very late on the brakes in the straight, I wasn't really catching up. It was terribly hard. Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing “In the end, it's not like Mexico used to be a track where you could overtake [previously]. With the temperatures, the altitude, everything is on fire once you're following someone.” Speaking before penalties were announced for Oscar Piastri , Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto – meaning he inherited ninth place after all – Hadjar could only see one positive from the race. item.title: Antonelli chooses Hamilton route over following Verstappen and Norris
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made his decision to continue racing with '12' in Formula 1 next season and will not take over '1' from McLaren's Lando Norris.” Antonelli became the youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, where he finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli is following the same approach as Hamilton. For next season, the Mercedes driver could have chosen to race with '1' as his number, but he will stick with '12' instead. Hamilton also kept '44' despite winning multiple world championships, while Verstappen and Norris both chose to race with '1'. Antonelli commented after the race: "I think I'll stay with number 12. I'll stay with number 12 because, obviously, it's a very special number for me, but also it's a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble, and I feel like by keeping number 12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve. "And also, to be honest, I'm very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I put it, it went extremely badly. So one more reason to stay with number 12. But, yeah, I will stay with number 12." Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen and Hamilton praise Antonelli Verstappen explained he is proud of the young Italian driver. He said: "Well, I think to achieve this in your second year in Formula 1 is always very impressive. Because, of course, at his age as well, to be so solid, not make big mistakes, and, of course, also beat your experienced teammate, he's just driven incredible. "And I'm very proud of him, how he has handled himself this whole season. It's not always easy to deliver every single weekend, but he has done that, and he's the deserved champion this year." Hamilton added: "It was beautiful to be up there with these two and to be up there with Kimi for his first World Championship. I think it was a very special moment, one of the most special moments that I remember having here."

But the lefty-hitting, Gold Glove left fielder lingered on the market until Jan. 21, when he agreed to a five-year, $162.5 million contract. That deal contains an opt out after the 2027 season, the start of which could be affected by a work stoppage. MLB’s current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, and a looming lockout will impact business over the next four weeks. And in this year’s free agent class, lefty-hitting Luis Arraez is a connoisseur of contact, with just 28 strikeouts in 655 plate appearances in 2026, while batting .310 for the Giants and Phillies . A three-time batting champ, Arraez – who turns 30 in April – came up with Minnesota in 2019, with James Rowson, then the Twins batting coach. item.description: Dermot Mee and Eoin Kenny are both underage internationals with Northern Ireland [Getty Images] Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot Mee and Portsmouth forward Eoin Kenny have been handed their first Northern Ireland call-ups for November's final Nations League matches with Ukraine and Hungary. Mee, 23, is a former Northern Ireland underage international and, although he has not played competitively for United this season, will add competition to NI's first choice goalkeeper Pierce Charles. Wide player Kenny, who is the son of former Republic of Ireland manager Stephen, joined Portsmouth from Dundalk in July. The 20-year-old has made one league appearance for the Championship club, but has been handed a first call up as Dion Charles, Eoin Toal and goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell drop out of the squad. Sunderland defender Dan Ballard is missing after he injured his hamstring in the September win over Georgia in Tbilisi, while midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell are also absent through injury. Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee. Family affair at Croke Park caps Mee's special night Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time. Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT before they travel to Hungary in their final match on 17 November. Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds. Northern Ireland are the only side left in the entire Nations League who have yet to concede a goal in this year's competition. Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner in Georgia in September before a goalless draw at home to Hungary. A 3-0 victory over Ukraine was one of the most impressive performances from O'Neill's young side, and they ended the quadruple-header with another goalless draw, this time at home to Georgia. If Northern Ireland can top the group they would not only win promotion to League A, but they would also be all but guaranteed of a play-off for Euro 2028. item.title: Di Gregorio set to remain in the Premier League beyond January
item.description: Di Gregorio set to remain in the Premier League beyond January Michele Di Gregorio is unlikely to leave Bournemouth during the January transfer window, despite previously being linked with a move to Bologna . The Serie A club had reportedly considered bringing the goalkeeper back to Italy, but their interest appears to have cooled in recent weeks. Di Gregorio joined the Premier League side at the start of this season on loan after Luciano Spalletti made it clear that he would not be Juventus’ first choice between the posts. The decision left the goalkeeper looking for an opportunity elsewhere, and Bournemouth offered him the chance to continue his career in England. His situation has not been straightforward, however, as he has mostly featured in cup competitions since arriving at the Cherries. Despite limited opportunities, he has continued working hard in training and remains determined to earn more minutes. Bologna interest appears to have faded Bologna were reportedly interested in signing Di Gregorio in January because they wanted to make him their first-choice goalkeeper. A return to Serie A could have offered him a clearer route to regular football, particularly given his current role at Bournemouth. However, according to Tuttomercatoweb , that possibility is now unlikely after the Italian side cooled their interest over recent weeks. The report indicates that Di Gregorio is expected to remain in England and complete his loan spell with Bournemouth this season. That development means the goalkeeper will have to continue competing for opportunities at his current club. Although he has not yet established himself as their number one, his commitment and performances have reportedly been appreciated by the club. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Bournemouth could make his move permanent The Cherries are said to be satisfied with Di Gregorio’s contributions so far and could look to turn his loan into a permanent transfer. Such a decision would represent a show of confidence in the goalkeeper, even though he has not yet secured a regular starting position. A permanent move could also give him greater stability as he attempts to establish himself in English football. Rather than having to consider another change of club after the current campaign, he would have the opportunity to focus on earning the trust of the coaching staff.

item.title: "My Granddad Got Me a City Shirt" - Elliot Anderson Opens Up on Childhood Affection for Manchester City
item.description: "My Granddad Got Me a City Shirt" - Elliot Anderson Opens Up on Childhood Affection for Manchester City Elliot Anderson has donned sky blue beneath Newcastle's black and white since childhood. Not every summer arrival hits the ground running, which makes City fans especially quick to warm to those players that do manage to slot right in. Summer signing Elliot Anderson certainly fits into that category. So far, adapting to life under Enzo Maresca has been smooth sailing, earning the midfielder acclaim from fans and pundits - and now a nomination for the Etihad Player of the Month award for October. Beyond his obvious impact on the pitch, the 23-year-old has quickly connected with supporters through his humility and sincerity when handling media duties away from the grass. After spending more than a decade in Newcastle United’s youth and senior ranks, followed by an impressive two-year spell at Nottingham Forest, the possessionally dominant style of Manchester City was always going to represent a major shift. However, the midfielder has taken the step in his stride and cites the instant backing he received from City supporters as a key factor in his swift acclimatisation. In a recent interview for the November edition of Manchester City's official magazine , Anderson discussed his enduring connection with the club and how backing from the terraces helped him move past a challenging debut. "The Manchester City fans have been great to me from the first minute I played and really supported me and got behind me," Anderson said. Obviously, my first game was in the Community Shield and wasn't my best performance, but I think the fans really sort of stuck with me and hopefully I’ve started to repay them." That bond has translated into stellar form on the pitch, with exceptional performances at Old Trafford and Anfield among the highlights. With Manchester City competing fiercely across domestic and European fronts, the midfielder's combative and composed displays have given Enzo Maresca a must-start name in the engine room. A childhood affinity for the Blues While Anderson's footballing education took place in the North East during his long association with Newcastle, his ties to the Blues do stretch back further than his recent transfer. Growing up with a soft spot for Manchester City, the midfielder revealed how a gift from his grandad during his childhood left a lasting impression. "I think I joined Newcastle U9s and left when I was about 21," the England midfielder added. "I was a long time at the club, and I loved it. "Obviously, I've always been a Newcastle fan, all my family have, but everyone has a second club and that was City for me. "My grandad got me a City shirt, I think around the 2010-11 season, and I was about eight at the time. It was something I’d just wear around the house - outside I was always in a Newcastle top." item.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas accuses Real Madrid of dragging out Negreira case to ruin Barcelona's reputation
item.description: GFX Javier Tebas Florentino Perez - Getty/GOAL La Liga president Javier Tebas has accused Real Madrid of intentionally prolonging the Negreira case to cause maximum reputational damage to Barcelona. The league chief suggests that the constant legal appeals from the capital are a strategic move to keep the scandal in the headlines. Tebas questions Madrid's motives Spanish courts are currently investigating payments made by Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Referees’ Technical Committee (CTA). While no evidence has proven sporting corruption, Los Blancos have aggressively targeted their Clasico rivals over the scandal . Tebas has now publicly condemned the capital club's approach. He claims their sudden interest in the investigation only began after Barcelona withdrew from the controversial European Super League project, accusing them of weaponising the legal system to hurt the Blaugrana. 'Stretching it like chewing gum' The league chief did not hold back when assessing Madrid's behaviour, suggesting paranoia has taken hold at the Bernabeu. "They are stretching the Negreira case like chewing gum. Real Madrid thinks Negreira is in every referee’s dressing room at every stadium where Real Madrid plays," Tebas stated during World In Progress (WIP) congress, as quoted by AS . "I remind Real Madrid that we went to the prosecutor’s office before Real Madrid did. The president of Real Madrid was on the board of directors for six months after the Negreira issue came to light. In a general assembly, he defended the club of his then-friend while it was in the Super League. The day Barca left, it seems everything changed." Unacceptable attacks on Barcelona Tebas believes the continued assault on Barcelona's public image is unwarranted while the judicial process is ongoing. "It must be clearly stated that what is happening with the constant attacks against Barcelona is unacceptable because this is a drawn-out affair," Tebas continued. "Barcelona will have to assume their responsibilities if necessary, but right now they cannot be blamed for anything because it is Real Madrid that is asking for the process to be prolonged." He concluded: "Barca’s case has nothing to do with Manchester City’s, and that cannot influence the justice system. The decision must be made here, in Spain." A Spanish resolution The Spanish judicial system will continue its investigation at its own pace, independently of other high-profile football cases across Europe. Tebas has explicitly distanced the Catalan club's situation from Manchester City's ongoing battle with the Premier League, insisting the verdict in England will not impact proceedings in Spain. Until a definitive legal conclusion is reached, the bitter off-pitch war of words between Spain's two biggest clubs shows no signs of slowing down.

item.title: ‘I stand by’… Bill Simmons doubles down on LA Lakers ownership group claims
item.description: Photo by Rebecca Sapp/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Podcaster Bill Simmons has doubled down on the claims he made about the Los Angeles Lakers . Earlier this year, Mark Walter made the surprise decision to sell the LA Lakers after little more than a year of ownership. A new ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner bought Walter out, but the deal is yet to be finalized. Last week, Bill Simmons caused a stir by claiming that the new group do not yet have the money to complete the buyout. ESPN has since reported that all terms of the deal have been agreed – but Simmons is sticking by his claims. Speaking on his most recent podcast, Simmons said: “They put out all these different pieces about they do have the money, but they didn’t actually say they had the money. “I see both sides. I think they’re confident they are gonna get the money. But I’ve talked to too many people who said they’re still looking to find the remaining money to pay $12.5 billion.” He added: “I think they probably will get the money, but I don’t think they have it yet because too many people have been shown the deck and offered it and offered a chance to get in.” Lakers sale is new record price The $12.5 billion agreement for the LA Lakers is a new record for a sports franchise, in excess of the $10 billion Walter paid in 2025. Simmons added: “It seems a little high. I’d kind of wanna own my own arena for $12.5bn. Anyway, I stand by what I said.” ESPN’s report said that Walter and Kushner have not yet signed a formal agreement, despite having a total agreement. item.title: Biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting Jens Berthel Askou
item.description: Biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting Jens Berthel Askou Charlie Mulgrew and Kevin Thomson have been discussing Martin O’Neill’s time at Celtic after a run of only three wins in ten matches has left the legendary manager facing calls from some supporters for him to stand aside… 1st November 2026; Falkirk Stadium, Scottish Premiership, Falkirk versus Celtic; Celtic manager Martin O’Neill. Photo Vagelis Georgariou And Thomson, speaking on The Breakdown podcast , made a very interesting point on what he regards as a huge opportunity Celtic missed out on during the summer when they passed on the chance to bring former Motherwell manager Jens Berthel Askou into the club to replace Martin O’Neill. Mulgrew pointed out that Martin O’Neill was just a stopgap and would give the club time to sort out all the issues in the background, including sourcing a Head of Recruitment, improving the stadium and so on. Martin O’Neill celebrating title victory. Thomson explained his point: “I do think, and it’s easy viewpoint on how it looked last year, I did think how dramatic the last day of the season was, he should’ve just up sticks and left. But I still felt the club would be missing a trick. “I think Martin would’ve been a brilliant foil, mentor or sounding board, somebody to speak to, somebody to confide in as part of whatever that looked like for Celtic, for the new manager coming in. “Now he’s been the manager; he’s had it for a longer period of time rather than just short-term, you kind of feel as though Martin O’Neill wouldn’t work because he’s now attached himself to being the manager.” Motherwell manager Jens Berthel Askou is seen during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Motherwell at Celtic Park on March 14, 2026.
